brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: Single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: Build is piece:0,0,0;half-n only - single cell at 0,0,0 level 0. Tested full, half and quarter variants; all are single-base compliant. Current build has no neighbours placed.

Configurator offers at most 1 drawer socket on any single base: full = 0 sockets, quarter = 0 sockets, half-n/half-s = 1 socket (key on cut face). Verified via find_sockets: after placing drawer:0#0,0#cut on half-n, no further drawer sockets offered. Five drawers cannot be placed without adding additional cells beside or below, which would violate the 'nothing else added beside or on top' constraint. Build shows maximum achievable: 1 drawer.

finish.summary: A single hex base can only accept 0-1 drawers depending on variant (full:0, half:1, quarter:0). Tested all variants; the configurator enforces one cut face per half base and thus one drawer max. Built the closest legal build: one half base with its single available drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut) to demonstrate the limit. Five drawers on one isolated base is not placeable.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
